management_questions: Is there a process to retrospectively obtain attendee details for flagged claims?
Are staff aware of the requirement to document attendees for entertainment expenses?
findings.observation: 198 of 234 entertainment-related claims (84.6%) are missing attendee information. The control objective is that entertainment claims must list attendees and business purpose, to demonstrate legitimate business use.
findings.recommendation: Mandate attendee fields as required for entertainment expense types in the expense system. Reject submissions without completed attendee details.
findings.title: Entertainment Claims Missing Attendee Details

findings.exposure_basis: Sum of this finding's own cited amount metric(s) ['duplicate_amount'] -- the same figure(s) rendered into its observation text, never re-derived from raw rows.
management_questions: What is the current process for detecting and resolving duplicate claims?
Have any of these duplicates already been identified and reversed?
findings.observation: 29 potential duplicate claim groups (60 lines, $1,994.79 at risk) were identified, of which 1 groups contain both an out-of-pocket and a corporate-card line for the same claim. Duplicate claims may result in double reimbursement, representing a potential financial loss pending confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Review all flagged duplicates and recover any confirmed double payments. Enhance duplicate detection logic in the expense system to prevent submission.
findings.title: Duplicate Expense Claims Identified

findings.observation: Of 799 expense reports reviewed by 11 approvers, 82.7% were approved without the approver viewing the receipt. Of the reports where the receipt was viewed, 4.1% were nonetheless approved within the instant-approval threshold of that viewing. 1 reports (0.1%) were approved with no receipt review at all, within the instant-approval threshold of when the approver received the report -- the highest-risk approval behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Implement minimum review time controls in the expense system. Require mandatory receipt viewing before approval submission. Establish approver review KPIs and include in performance discussions.
findings.title: Inadequate Approver Review of Expense Reports

management_questions: Is there a follow-up process for pre-approved travel that doesn't result in an expense report?
What percentage of these represent cancelled travel vs missing expense reports?
findings.observation: 85 pre-approved travel requests totalling $182,552.32 across 10 employees do not have linked expense reports. This may indicate travel that was approved but not taken, or expense reports that were not properly linked to pre-approvals.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile unlinked travel requests with actual travel records. Implement automated matching between pre-approvals and expense reports.
findings.title: Travel Requests Without Linked Expense Reports

management_questions: What additional controls exist for high-value expense claims?
Have any of these high-value claims been subject to post-approval review?
findings.observation: 38 claims exceed the high-value threshold, totalling $318,785.60 across 10 employees. High-value claims carry elevated risk of misuse and warrant additional review beyond standard approval workflows.
findings.recommendation: Implement tiered approval for high-value claims, requiring secondary sign-off from finance. Conduct periodic deep-dive reviews of high-value transactions.
findings.title: High-Value Claims Requiring Enhanced Scrutiny

management_questions: Is team entertainment (e.g., team lunches) a legitimate and expected expense for ExCo?
Should direct-report entertainment require separate approval from the next level?
findings.observation: 3 of 4 entertainment-entry attendee records have attendees within the claimant's reporting hierarchy. The control objective is that entertainment attendees should not be within the claimant's reporting hierarchy, to prevent self-serving approvals.
findings.recommendation: Implement hierarchical validation in the expense system to flag claims where attendees are within the claimant's reporting hierarchy. Require next-level-up approval for such claims.
findings.title: Attendee Hierarchy Validity Exceptions

findings.exposure_basis: Sum of this finding's own cited amount metric(s) ['daily_over_amount_dom', 'daily_over_amount_int'] -- the same figure(s) rendered into its observation text, never re-derived from raw rows.
management_questions: Are there legitimate business scenarios that would exceed the daily per-diem in a single day?
Should the daily limit be adjusted for international travel days?
What controls exist to prevent excessive single-day spend?
findings.observation: 2 domestic and 2 international employee-days exceeded the applicable per-diem daily spend threshold, totalling $446.40 and $998.53 respectively in excess spend. The highest single domestic day was $437.92 and the highest single international day was $814.25. Concentrated single-day spend may reflect legitimate exceptional circumstances, or may warrant review against the control objective.
findings.recommendation: Review high daily-spend instances to verify business purpose. Consider implementing real-time daily spend caps with automatic escalation for amounts exceeding policy limits.
findings.title: Daily Spend Limit Exceedances

management_questions: Are all ExCo members and their delegates aware of the pre-approval requirement?
Should certain expense types (e.g., local meals) be exempt from pre-approval?
findings.observation: 8 bookings (2 employees) have no matching travel request on file. The control objective is that all travel should be pre-approved before expenses are incurred, to support budgetary control and management oversight. This name-and-class join matched 33.3% of bookings to a travel request overall; a lower match rate limits how completely this test can rely on the join, and is not itself a measure of compliance.
findings.recommendation: Enforce pre-approval requirements in the expense system by blocking submission without a linked travel request. For each flagged booking, confirm whether a matching travel request exists under a different name or class before treating the absence of a match as non-compliance.
findings.title: Employees Submitting Claims Without Pre-Approval

management_questions: What is the estimated cost impact of non-preferred supplier usage?
Are there legitimate reasons (e.g., route availability) for the non-preferred bookings?
findings.observation: 1 domestic and 20 international airline bookings, and 1 domestic and 0 international car rental bookings, used non-preferred suppliers (accommodation not assessed -- no preferred-hotel list supplied). Use of non-preferred suppliers foregoes negotiated corporate rates and volume discounts, which may increase travel costs.
findings.recommendation: Reinforce preferred supplier policy and ensure the corporate booking tool defaults to preferred suppliers. Require justification for non-preferred bookings exceeding a cost threshold.
findings.title: Non-Preferred Supplier Usage

management_questions: What is the current policy for handling claims without receipts?
Are there legitimate reasons for the volume of missing receipts (e.g., system issues)?
findings.observation: 27 claims (0.7% of total) are missing receipt documentation, representing $1,009.26 in unsupported spend, of which 0 have no affidavit on file. Without receipts, the business purpose and legitimacy of these expenses cannot be independently verified.
findings.recommendation: Enforce mandatory receipt attachment before expense report submission. Implement automated rejection for claims exceeding $50.00 without supporting documentation.

source_ref.basis: Sum of every 'approved_not_spent' finding's own exposure_amount -- money authorised (e.g. an approved travel request) but never turned into an actual reimbursed transaction. Reported separately because it is not spend at all; never included in the gross-flagged-spend headline above.
source_ref.label: Approved but never spent (not flagged spend)

source_ref.basis: The amount at risk: every distinct flagged transaction line counts exactly once, at the largest amount any finding attributes to it. A finding that flags a full spend amount counts the line's own full value; a finding that flags only an excess over a limit counts only the at-risk portion (for example the extra lines beyond the first in a duplicate group, or the part of a per-diem day's spend that is over the daily limit, allocated pro rata to that day's lines). Line identity is the row's own identity for a one-row-per-entry source, or a repeats-grain key declared in the Skill's source contract where one source row is genuinely the same business entry as another (e.g. one row per attendee of one entertainment claim). Findings for money that was approved but never spent are excluded here and reported separately as approved-but-unspent; findings with no dollar figure are also excluded. Per-finding exposure figures overlap with each other and with this headline by design (the same line can be cited by more than one finding) and must never be summed.
source_ref.label: Potential exposure
